content.user_title: Verify Private AI Inference with NEAR AI Cloud
content.value_statement: Private AI integrations need clear guidance for trusted inference and attestation checks. This skill provides implementation and verification workflows for NEAR AI Cloud.
actual_capabilities: Configures OpenAI-compatible clients for the NEAR AI Cloud API.
Explains model and gateway attestation retrieval.
Guides validation of NVIDIA NRAS and Intel TDX attestation evidence.
Explains nonce freshness and GPU-to-CPU binding checks.
Describes signed chat message verification workflows.
Compares private and anonymised inference request patterns.
limitations: Does not operate NEAR AI Cloud or issue API credentials.
Does not independently prove vendor privacy, pricing, or model claims.
Requires current vendor documentation and trusted verification libraries.
Does not replace application-specific threat modeling or key management.

use_cases.title: Build private inference clients
use_cases.description: Configure an OpenAI-compatible client and send requests to NEAR AI Cloud with a user-provided API key.

use_cases.title: Review attestation evidence
use_cases.description: Validate attestation reports, nonce freshness, certificate chains, and GPU-to-CPU bindings before trusting inference.

use_cases.title: Design signed chat workflows
use_cases.description: Plan how to retrieve and verify signatures for chat messages that need an audit trail.

prompt_templates.title: Start an API client
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to configure an OpenAI-compatible client for NEAR AI Cloud. Use environment variables for my API key.

prompt_templates.title: Request model attestation
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how to request a model attestation report with a fresh nonce and identify fields I must validate.

prompt_templates.title: Verify TEE evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a verification checklist for NVIDIA NRAS and Intel TDX evidence, including GPU-to-CPU key binding.

prompt_templates.title: Plan trusted chat records
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a signed chat audit workflow. Cover message binding, signature retrieval, verification, expiry, and key rotation.

output_examples.input: What must I verify before trusting a model attestation?
output: Validate issuer, signature, certificate chain, measurements, expiry, and nonce match.
Confirm GPU, CPU, and signing-key bindings.

output_examples.input: How should I store my NEAR AI Cloud key?
output_examples.output: Store it in a secret manager or environment variable. Do not commit it, log it, or include it in client-side code.

output_examples.input: When should I use signed chat verification?
output_examples.output: Use it when chat content needs integrity evidence, traceability, or an audit record. Verify each signature against expected message data.

best_practices: Generate a new cryptographic nonce for every attestation request.
Validate signatures, issuers, expiry, measurements, and binding claims with trusted libraries.
Keep API keys in secret storage and send only intended data to approved endpoints.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a decoded JWT as a verified attestation.
Do not reuse nonces or skip GPU-to-CPU binding validation.
Do not paste API keys or sensitive production tokens into logs, examples, or third-party tools.

faq.question: What does this skill support?
faq.answer: It provides guidance for NEAR AI Cloud clients, attestation verification, signed chat checks, and encrypted chat workflows.

faq.question: Does this skill provide an API key?
faq.answer: No. You must obtain and manage your own NEAR AI Cloud credentials.

faq.question: Can I use an OpenAI SDK?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill describes configuring an OpenAI-compatible base URL and API key for NEAR AI Cloud.

faq.question: Why is a nonce required?
faq.answer: A fresh nonce helps bind attestation evidence to your request and reduces replay risk.

faq.question: Is decoding a JWT enough?
faq.answer: No. You must validate its signature, issuer, expiry, audience, and required attestation claims.

faq.question: Does attestation replace application security?
faq.answer: No. You still need key management, input controls, endpoint validation, logging policy, and threat modeling.
